facts: In this appeal by special leave, the learned counsel for the appellants has pressed the appeal only on the question of the applicability of S. 302 read with S. 149 IPC to the appellants other than Ramakant Rai.
The occurrence took place in the disputed field which was claimed by both the parties.

There was exchange of brickbats and ultimately one of the accused Ram Sewak who was armed with a gun, fired a shot which hit the right eye of Janardan as a result of which he fell down and died instantaneously.
Although some of the appellants were armed with pharsa and spear and one of the appellants with a pistol, but none of these weapons were used.
The appellants have served only 3 to 4 months and have been on bail throughout.
For these reasons, therefore, we after the conviction of the appellants except Ramakant Rai from one under Section 302/149 to Section 325/149
In lieu of sentence remitted, we impose a fine of Rs. 5000 on each of the appellants in default to two years' R. I.
The entire fine, if realised, shall be paid to PW 1, the widow of Janardan.
issues: What is the applicability of S. 302 read with S. 149 IPC to the appellants other than Ramakant Rai?
petitioner_arguments: According to the findings of the Court below, the occurrence took place in the disputed field which was claimed by both the parties.
The conclusion is inescapable that Ram Sewak and Ramakant Rai and undoubtedly the common intention to cause murder of the deceased.
There can be no doubt that the appellants had gone armed in order to dispossess the prosecution party and cause such injury as may be necessary for achieving that object.
court_reasoning: The conclusion is inescapable that Ram Sewak and Ramakant Rai and undoubtedly the common intention to cause murder of the deceased.

In the circumstances of the present case, there can be no doubt that the appellants had gone armed in order to dispossess the prosecution party and cause such injury as may be necessary for achieving that object.
But this question depends on the facts of each case.
The other question that has to be determined is as to what sentence should be awarded to the appellants.
holding: Fine to be paid in six months.
After the fine is paid, the appellants shall be discharged from bail bonds.
Ramakant Rai is convicted under Section 302/34 and his sentence of life imprisonment is upheld under this section.
The sentence u/s. 147 is also reduced to the period already undergone.
